walk.enumeration: Read-only GitHub GraphQL, for every repository in pool.json: repository(owner, name) { pullRequests(first: 25, orderBy: {field: CREATED_AT, direction: DESC}) { nodes { number url createdAt state mergedAt isDraft title baseRefOid headRefOid } } }, paged until a page held a pull request created before window_start. Changed files per pull request: pullRequest(number) { files(first: 100) { nodes { path changeType } } }, paged.
walk.cross_check: GitHub issue search, is:pr created:>=2026-10-02 repo:<a> repo:<b> ... over 60-repository chunks (415 requests). Every pull request it returned is in the GraphQL list except 7 created on 2026-11-17 after their repositories were listed; the GraphQL list's extra pull requests come from search's 1,000-result cap (jsboige/CoursIA, hushh-labs/hushh-research) and from renamed repositories, which repo: search does not follow.
walk.unresolved_note: GitHub answered NOT_FOUND for 145 pool repositories (deleted, private or otherwise unavailable on the walk date); none of their pull requests could be listed.
walk.renamed_note: 41 pool repositories now answer under another name; their pull requests are listed under the pool name in `repository`, with GitHub's current URL in `url`.
walk.pins: merge_base is git merge-base of the pull request's baseRefOid and headRefOid; head is headRefOid as listed on 2026-11-17. Both were fetched into a blobless clone (git clone --filter=blob:none).
walk.method: For each candidate, the patch and the files it touches were read at both pins, with the agent constructions and imports around them. AST scripts listed every Agent, LlmAgent, SequentialAgent, ParallelAgent, LoopAgent and RealtimeAgent construction with its tools, handoffs, sub_agents and mcp_servers arguments; every changed function (its AST without the docstring); and the modules that files importing the OpenAI Agents SDK or Google ADK import. The judge read by hand every candidate those facts linked to an agent, and reviewed the rest from their changed files. No Agents Shipgate command was run on any candidate.
walk.order_note: The window's large repositories finished listing after the candidates of smaller repositories had been judged, so 99 candidates created after the 30th member were also judged; they are not part of the walk and are not listed.
interpretations: Pool: the repositories named in pool.json, followed through GitHub's redirect when renamed; a repository GitHub no longer serves contributes no candidate.

Candidates (step 3): state as listed on 2026-11-17 (a draft is open); the patch edits a non-test .py file when GitHub's file list for the pull request holds a .py path, added, modified, removed or renamed, that is not test code by the engine's own convention: a `test` or `tests` directory, or a test_*.py, *_test.py, conftest.py, test.py or tests.py file.
Step 2's package exclusion is decided per candidate at its merge base; such candidates are listed as skipped with that reason (openai/openai-agents-python, google/adk-python).

A tool's own code is its function's AST without the docstring, decorators and defaults included, as the implementation digest covers: comment, formatting and docstring-only edits are not changes, and neither is code the tool calls. Where a tool is built as FunctionTool(on_invoke_tool=f), f is the bound function.

Tools bound as objects are bindings, as the engine reads them: an MCP toolset whose tool filter or allowlist admits or drops tools adds or removes those tools; code inside an MCP server, or inside the toolset object, is not a bound function's own code.
Deleting an agent that exists at the merge base removes its tools, handoffs and sub-agents; a removal describes the deleted source path, as the engine's removal does.
An agent constructed only at the head is new, not an agent that exists at the merge base, whatever it binds.

Application code includes samples, tutorials, demos, showcases and book code, as the development corpus did. Code that implements an agent framework, SDK, library, instrumentation, adapter, template or evaluation harness is not; nor is a platform whose agents take their tools from runtime configuration, where no binding exists in source.

The framework is read off the constructor's import: OpenAI Agents SDK means the `agents` package that is the SDK (SandboxAgent and RealtimeAgent included), never a local package named agents; Google ADK means google.adk. LiveKit, Strands, Pydantic AI, CrewAI, Microsoft Agent Framework and repositories' own agent classes are neither.
A runtime configuration file the application reads to build a list (FlySecAgent's mcp.json) is input to the list, not a binding written in code.
A member held only under a condition (a configuration flag, a token being present) is still a binding change when the condition or the list holding it changes.
